topics: 👑 The Eighteen-Year-Old Nasi — Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's white hair, the open doors, and the benches added 'on that day'
🌍 Yehuda the Ammonite Convert — Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua debate whether Sennacherib scrambled the nations
🤝 Reconciliation — the blacksmith's walls, 'for my father's honor', and how both Sages kept the office
⏰ Mussaf and Minḥa — negligence, which comes first, the curse of 'nugei', and eating before prayer
🙏 Prayers of the Study Hall — Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana, and the deathbed words of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai
🔢 Why Eighteen Blessings? — Psalm 29, Shema, the spine, and the nineteenth blessing instituted at Yavne

overview.title: 📖 Overview: A Day That Changed the Study Hall
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 28a–28b
overview.hebrewSource: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאָמְרִינַן ״בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם״ — הַהוּא יוֹמָא הֲוָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The story of Rabban Gamliel's removal continues: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya accepts the post, the doorkeeper is dismissed, hundreds of benches are added, and Eduyyot is taught that very day. Rabban Gamliel does not stay away — he debates Rabbi Yehoshua over an Ammonite convert, loses, and goes to make peace. The daf then returns to the mishna's timing of Mussaf: which prayer comes first when both are pending, what befalls one who prays late, and whether one may eat before Mussaf or Minḥa. A new mishna brings Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana's prayers on entering and leaving the study hall, followed by the final teachings of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai. Finally the mishna on the Amida opens, and the Gemara asks why there are eighteen blessings — and why there are really nineteen.

slides.title: 👑 From Deposition to Shared Leadership
slides.subtitle: How Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya took office, and how Rabban Gamliel returned

steps.content: 1️⃣ His wife warns: 'Perhaps they will remove you too.' He answers with a proverb: use the precious goblet today even if it breaks tomorrow. 'You have no white hair' — he is eighteen, and eighteen rows of hair turn white. Hence: 'I am as one seventy years old'

2️⃣ The doorkeeper is dismissed and all students may enter, reversing Rabban Gamliel's rule that only a student whose inside is like his outside (תּוֹכוֹ כְּבָרוֹ) may enter. Four hundred, or seven hundred, benches are added
3️⃣ Rabban Gamliel is disheartened: 'Perhaps I withheld Torah from Israel.' He dreams of white jugs full of ashes — but the Gemara says this was shown only to ease his mind
4️⃣ Eduyyot was taught that day; every 'on that day' (בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם) refers to it; no pending halakha went unresolved. Rabban Gamliel did not absent himself even for an hour

5️⃣ Rabban Gamliel goes to appease Rabbi Yehoshua, sees his blackened walls: 'You are a blacksmith!' — 'Woe to a generation whose leader does not know how scholars make a living.' Forgiven only 'for my father's honor'

6️⃣ A launderer carries word; Rabbi Yehoshua's message: 'the one who wears the uniform shall wear it.' Rabbi Akiva locks the gates. Rabbi Yehoshua comes himself: 'the sprinkler, son of a sprinkler, shall sprinkle'

7️⃣ Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya cannot be demoted — one elevates in sanctity and does not lower (מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵין מוֹרִידִין). Rabban Gamliel lectures three weeks, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya one. The student who started it all: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai

callout.label: Ḥagiga echo:
callout.text: This arrangement explains the phrase 'Whose week was it? It was Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's week.'

slides.title: 🌍 May Yehuda the Ammonite Enter the Congregation?
slides.subtitle: Rabban Gamliel, though deposed, joins the halakhic debate — and loses

lines.speaker: Yehuda
lines.text: What is my status for entering the congregation of Israel?

lines.speaker: R. Gamliel
lines.text: You are forbidden. 'An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord' (Deuteronomy 23:4).

lines.speaker: R. Yehoshua
lines.text: Do Ammon and Moab still sit in their place? Sennacherib came and scrambled all the nations — 'I have removed the bounds of the peoples' (Isaiah 10:13). And whatever separates, separates from the majority (כׇּל דְּפָרֵישׁ מֵרוּבָּא פָּרֵישׁ).

lines.speaker: R. Gamliel
lines.text: But it says 'afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon' (Jeremiah 49:6) — and they have already returned!

lines.speaker: R. Yehoshua
lines.text: It also says 'I will turn the captivity of My people Israel' (Amos 9:14) — and they have not yet returned. Only proven facts count.

lines.speaker: Result
lines.text: They immediately permitted him to enter the congregation. Rabban Gamliel concluded: since the people follow Rabbi Yehoshua, I should go and appease him.

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: Rabbi Yehoshua combines a historical fact (population transfer) with a legal presumption (follow the majority) — the individual convert is assumed to come from the permitted majority of nations.

slides.title: ⏰ Mussaf, Minḥa, and the Cost of Delay
slides.subtitle: Rulings that follow from 'the additional prayer may be recited all day'
rows: Mussaf 'all day' — no penalty for delay?
Rabbi Yoḥanan: one who postpones it is nevertheless called negligent (פּוֹשֵׁעַ)
Delay is permitted but faulted
Both Minḥa and Mussaf pending — which first?
Rabbis: Minḥa, the frequent one; Rabbi Yehuda: Mussaf, whose time is elapsing
Rabbi Yoḥanan: Minḥa first — Rabbi Natan bar Tovi learned this from him forty times
Mussaf after seven hours (per Rabbi Yehuda)
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi applies 'nugei' (Zephaniah 3:18) = destruction, per Rav Yosef's Targum on delaying the Festivals
A grave failing
Shaḥarit after four hours (per Rabbi Yehuda)
Rabbi Elazar applies the same verse; 'nugei' = sorrow, from Psalms 119:28 and Lamentations 1:4
A grave failing
May one eat before Mussaf?
Rav Huna: forbidden — this is why sick Rav Avya skipped Rav Yosef's lecture
Halakha is not like Rav Huna
May one eat once Minḥa's time arrives?
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: forbidden
Halakha is not like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
May an individual pray before the congregation?
Rabbi Yoḥanan: forbidden; Rabbi Abba: only when he is with the congregation
Abaye: Rav Avya could have prayed Mussaf alone at home

callout.label: Rabbi Zeira's doorway:
callout.text: Tired from study, Rabbi Zeira sat at Rabbi Natan bar Tovi's door to rise for passing scholars and earn a mitzva. There he confirmed that the Minḥa-first ruling was truly Rabbi Yoḥanan's and not Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's.

slides.title: 🙏 Three Prayers of the Study Hall and the Deathbed
slides.subtitle: The mishna: Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana prayed briefly on entering and on leaving

boxes.title: On entering
items: 'May no mishap come about through me (שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי)'
That I not fail in a matter of halakha, and my colleagues rejoice in me
That I not call the impure pure or the pure impure
That my colleagues not fail, and I rejoice in them

boxes.title: On leaving
items: 'I thank You that You placed my lot among those who sit in the study hall, not on street corners'
I rise early — for Torah; they rise early — for idle matters
I toil and receive reward; they toil and do not
I run to the World-to-Come; they run to the pit of destruction

boxes.title: Final teachings
items: Rabbi Eliezer: honor your colleagues, keep your children from higgayon, seat them at scholars' knees, and when you pray, know before Whom you stand
Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai weeps: a mortal king's anger, prison, and death are temporary and he can be appeased — the King of Kings' are eternal, and two paths lie before me
His blessing: 'May the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood.' 'Only that much?' 'Would that it were! A sinner says: let no man see me'
At the end: clear the vessels from impurity, and set a chair for Hezekiah, King of Judah, who is coming

callout.label: Common thread:
callout.text: Each prayer measures a person's life against the presence of God — in learning, in idleness, and at the threshold of judgment.

slides.title: 🔢 Eighteen Blessings — Corresponding to What?
slides.subtitle: The mishna: Rabban Gamliel says the full eighteen daily; Rabbi Yehoshua an abridged form; Rabbi Akiva — full only if fluent

nodes.content: ❓ On what did the Sages base the number eighteen (שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה)?

columns.label: R. Hillel b. R. Shmuel
columns.content: The eighteen mentions of God's name in David's 'Give unto the Lord, O sons of might' (Psalm 29)

columns.label: Rav Yosef
columns.content: The eighteen mentions of God's name in the Shema

columns.label: R. Tanḥum / RYbL
columns.content: The eighteen vertebrae of the spine — so one bows until every vertebra protrudes

nodes.content: ⚠️ But are these eighteen? They are nineteen!

💡 Rabbi Levi: the blessing of the heretics (בִּרְכַּת הַמִּינִים) was instituted later at Yavne. Its counterpart: 'the God of glory thunders' (Ps. 29:3); the word 'One' in Shema; the small vertebra at the base of the spine
📜 Shimon HaPakuli arranged the eighteen in order before Rabban Gamliel at Yavne. 'Who can compose the blessing of the heretics?' Shmuel HaKatan stood and composed it — and the next year he forgot it

callout.label: How low to bow:
callout.text: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: until the vertebrae protrude. Ulla: until one could see a small coin (issar) opposite his heart. Rabbi Ḥanina: once the head is moved forward it is enough. Rava: only if he strains and appears to be bowing.

summary.principle: The day Rabban Gamliel was deposed opened the study hall to all and resolved every pending halakha — and Rabban Gamliel, humbled in debate, made peace, so that both Sages shared the office.

flowSteps.content: 👑 Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, eighteen with white hair, becomes Nasi; the door is opened and benches multiply
🌍 Rabban Gamliel debates Rabbi Yehoshua over the Ammonite convert and loses → he seeks forgiveness at the blacksmith's house
🤝 One elevates in sanctity and does not lower: Rabban Gamliel three weeks, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya one

columns.content: ⏰ Minḥa before Mussaf (Rabbi Yoḥanan); halakha permits eating before Mussaf and Minḥa
🙏 Neḥunya ben Hakana's prayers; 'know before Whom you stand'; fear Heaven as you fear man

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: the eighteen blessings mirror Psalm 29, the Shema, and the spine; the nineteenth, against heretics, was added at Yavne by Shmuel HaKatan

quiz.q: How did Rabbi Yehoshua answer Rabban Gamliel's proof from 'an Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation'?
o: The verse applies only to Moabites, not Ammonites
Sennacherib scrambled the nations, so today's Ammonites are not ethnic Ammonites, and we follow the majority
Converts are never included in the prohibition
The prohibition lapsed after the destruction of the Temple
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua cited Isaiah 10:13 on Sennacherib's population transfers and the principle that whatever separates is presumed to come from the majority. When Rabban Gamliel cited Ammon's return (Jeremiah 49:6), he replied that Israel's return (Amos 9:14) has also not yet happened.

quiz.q: Why was Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya not simply removed when Rabban Gamliel was restored?
o: Because he had been appointed for life
Because the Sages feared his wealth
Because one elevates in sanctity and does not lower
Because Rabban Gamliel refused to return without him
quiz.e: The tradition 'one elevates in sanctity and does not lower' prevented demoting him. Alternating weekly would breed jealousy, so Rabban Gamliel lectured three weeks and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya one.

quiz.q: If both Minḥa and Mussaf are pending, which is recited first according to the halakha as ruled by Rabbi Yoḥanan?
o: Mussaf, because its time is about to elapse
Minḥa, because it is the more frequent prayer
Whichever the person prefers
Mussaf, because it corresponds to a sacrifice
quiz.e: The Rabbis hold that the frequent practice takes precedence, so Minḥa comes first; Rabbi Yehuda prefers Mussaf since its time elapses. Rabbi Yoḥanan ruled like the Rabbis, a ruling Rabbi Natan bar Tovi learned from him forty times.

quiz.q: When Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai blessed his students that their fear of Heaven be like their fear of flesh and blood, they asked 'only that much?' What did he answer?
o: That fearing God more than man is impossible for humans
Would that you reached that level — a sinner says only 'let no man see me'
That fear of man is greater than fear of God
That he was too weak to bless them further
quiz.e: He explained that people sin when they think no human is watching. If one feared God as much as he fears being seen by others, he would never sin — so the blessing is actually a high standard.

quiz.q: The Gemara notes that the 'eighteen' blessings are really nineteen. How does Rabbi Levi resolve this?
o: Two of the blessings were originally one
The blessing of the heretics was instituted later at Yavne
The nineteenth is only recited on Shabbat
Psalm 29 actually mentions God's name nineteen times
quiz.e: Rabbi Levi explains that the blessing of the heretics was added at Yavne, where Shmuel HaKatan composed it at Rabban Gamliel's request. Each of the three correspondences is then extended to cover the nineteenth blessing.
